newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico 1997 bank loans to farms seen up 27 pct.
newsitem.headline: Mexico 1997 bank loans to farms seen up 27 pct.

text.p: The Mexican banking system in 1997 will set aside 56.749 billion pesos for financing to the farm sector, Oscar Terroba, the general director of the rural development bank Banrural, said on Tuesday.

"For 1997, commercial and development banks will channel 56.749 billion pesos (to support rural financing), an amount 27 percent higher than was delivered in 1996," Terroba said during a presentation of the government's Rural Alliance program.
Terroba said that of that total, 45.817 billion pesos or about 80 percent would come from development banks.

He said the financing would lead to the planting of 12.35 million acres (five million hectares) of farmland and the purchase of 700,000 head of cattle to benefit a total of 1.2 million agricultural producers.

In 1996, commercial and development banks delivered 43.565 billion pesos worth of credits to the agricultural sector, Terroba said. Under those figures the increase from 1996 to 1997 would be about 30 percent, but Terroba did not explain how the numbers were calculated.
Of the 1996 financing, 80 percent also came from development banks, he said.
